topics.name: Interview Foundations
topics.description: Evidence-based preparation and concise interview responses.

module.title: Career Readiness Fundamentals
module.description: A short pilot covering workplace messages, evidence-backed stories, and interview preparation.

body.summary: Frame a professional message around context, requested action, owner, and deadline.
body.practice: Rewrite a vague follow-up so the recipient can act without another clarification.

body.summary: Describe a situation, your action, and a verifiable result without exaggeration.
body.practice: Turn one project experience into a concise situation-action-result story.

body.summary: Map role requirements to truthful examples, questions, and a practical rehearsal plan.
body.practice: Choose two requirements and pair each with one evidence story.

questions.prompt: Which follow-up makes the requested action clearest?

options.text: Please confirm the two budget figures by 3 PM Thursday so I can submit the plan.

questions.explanation: The request names the action, scope, deadline, and purpose.

questions.prompt: What is the best first sentence when reporting a missed deadline?

options.text: The deliverable will be one day late; I own the delay and will send the verified file by 11 AM tomorrow.
Things happened, but it should be fine.

questions.explanation: It states the impact, accountability, and a concrete recovery commitment.

questions.prompt: Which detail should be removed from a concise status update?

options.text: A long chronology that does not change the decision.

questions.explanation: A status update should preserve decision-relevant context and remove unrelated chronology.

options.text: I am always a great leader.
I reorganized weekly triage, cutting unresolved requests from 18 to 6 in four weeks.

questions.explanation: It connects a specific action to a bounded, verifiable result.

questions.prompt: How should you handle a requirement you have not performed before?

options.text: State the gap honestly, connect transferable evidence, and explain how you would learn.

questions.explanation: Truthful transferable evidence and a learning plan preserve credibility.

questions.prompt: Which preparation step best improves answer quality?

options.text: Memorize one answer for every role.
Map each priority requirement to a truthful evidence story and rehearse concise delivery.
Use claims that cannot be checked.

questions.explanation: Role-specific mapping produces relevant and supportable answers.
